$comment: STATIC COPY for Finance. Labels, tones, meanings, formulas and cautions — the words the module speaks. This is NOT placeholder data awaiting an endpoint: when the API arrives it serves the same list from GET /admin/finance/vocabularies, and the panel keeps reading it from one place so a state cannot be spelled one way on a list and another way on a record. Every metric and every KPI carries its own formula and its own caution, rendered behind an i button, because the only defence against one number meaning two different things six months apart is writing down what it means next to it.
moduleRule: Finance RECORDS TRANSACTIONS. Four things get recorded and nothing else: a subscription sale and its installments, a salary, a company expense or income, a refund. Every row exists because something happened — money moved, a gateway declined, a due date passed. No state here means "recorded but not yet believed". Finance does not decide what is owed either; Invoice does that, and Deals holds the balance.

recordTypes.label: Subscriptions
recordTypes.help: Business subscriptions: activated against the invoice raised for them, paid in installments. The installment is the unit that gets paid.

recordTypes.label: Salaries A/C
recordTypes.help: What each team member is paid, attached to their Team record, issued as a numbered slip they can be handed.

recordTypes.label: Other Transaction
recordTypes.help: Company money out and in under a tag you create. Everything that is not a subscription and not a salary.

recordTypes.label: Refunds
recordTypes.help: Money going back out — against a subscription payment, or raised by hand. The only routine action that sends money out of the company.

recordTypes.label: Analytics
recordTypes.help: The four record types read back as one picture, and the KPIs that turn it into a decision.

subscriptionSources.label: Sales
subscriptionSources.help: A salesperson closed it on a deal and recorded the payment against the invoice. Carries a deal reference.

subscriptionSources.label: Website
subscriptionSources.help: The customer bought it themselves and paid through the gateway. No salesperson, which is why it costs nothing to acquire beyond the ad spend.

installmentStatuses.label: Paid
installmentStatuses.meaning: The money arrived and is in the ledger. The receipt is issued and it counts as collected.

installmentStatuses.label: Due
installmentStatuses.meaning: Nothing has happened to it yet. This is the absence of an event, not a claim about one — it is not late until its due date passes.

installmentStatuses.label: Fail to pay
installmentStatuses.meaning: A real failure, recorded with its evidence: a gateway declined it, a mandate was cancelled, or the due date passed with nothing against it. Never a guess.

installmentStatuses.label: Cancelled
installmentStatuses.meaning: The installment will not be collected. The subscription was ended, or its invoice was cancelled.

$comment_installmentStatuses: FAIL TO PAY IS A FACT, NOT A DOUBT. It records something that actually occurred and stores the evidence in `failure` — a gateway response code, or a due date that has demonstrably passed. It is the one status on this page that looks like a judgement and is not one.

failureReasons.label: Declined by the bank
failureReasons.help: The gateway returned a decline. The card or account exists; the payment was refused.

failureReasons.label: Insufficient funds
failureReasons.help: The account did not hold the amount on the day it was attempted.

failureReasons.label: Mandate cancelled
failureReasons.help: The standing instruction was withdrawn, so nothing was even attempted.

failureReasons.label: Due date passed
failureReasons.help: No attempt and no payment. The date is the evidence — nothing was collected and the day has gone.

subscriptionStatuses.label: Active
subscriptionStatuses.meaning: Running, with installments still to come.

subscriptionStatuses.label: Completed
subscriptionStatuses.meaning: Every installment paid and the term served.

subscriptionStatuses.label: Defaulting
subscriptionStatuses.meaning: At least one installment failed and has not been recovered. The money is not coming on its own.

subscriptionStatuses.label: Cancelled
subscriptionStatuses.meaning: Ended early. Remaining installments are cancelled, not written off.

subscriptionStatuses.label: Refunded
subscriptionStatuses.meaning: Money paid on it has gone back out. The counter-entries are on the record.

salaryRunStates.label: Open
salaryRunStates.meaning: The month is not finished. Slips can still be adjusted; nobody has been paid.

salaryRunStates.label: Paid
salaryRunStates.meaning: The transfers were made and recorded. Every slip in the run is frozen.

$comment_salaryRunStates: A run is being prepared or it happened — there is no approval state, because paying salaries is not a claim anybody verifies afterwards. `open` is not a pending decision: it means the calendar month is still running.
slipRule: A slip freezes its own earnings and deductions. They are copied onto it, never read through to the salary account — so a raise next month cannot silently rewrite last month's slip. Gross is the sum of the earnings on the slip, net is gross minus the deductions on the slip, and neither is ever CTC divided by twelve.

tagKinds.label: Fixed
tagKinds.help: Runs whether or not anything is sold: rent, tools, utilities.

tagKinds.label: Reinvestment
tagKinds.help: Spend that buys customers. It is the CAC numerator, which is why the tag has to be right.

tagKinds.label: Variable
tagKinds.help: Scales with delivery: vendors, contractors, fulfilment.

tagKinds.label: Excluded
tagKinds.landsIn: Cash out, not an operating cost
tagKinds.help: Taxes and statutory payments. Money leaves, the operating picture does not change.

$comment_tagKinds: TAGS ARE CUSTOM — anyone with edit rights creates one. What is NOT free is the kind: it is chosen at creation and it decides where the money lands in analytics. A tag is deactivated, never deleted, because deleting one would silently re-bucket every transaction that already used it.
$comment_manualCreditKinds: The ONLY three credits a person may hand-key, and all three are flagged non-revenue. Customer money has exactly one way in: a subscription. If anyone could type a credit, anyone could fabricate revenue.

transactionStates.label: Recorded
transactionStates.meaning: The money moved. There is no draft state on this page — a row here means it happened.

transactionStates.label: Reversed
transactionStates.meaning: A counter-entry was appended. The original row is untouched and still on the record.

refundOrigins.label: Against a subscription
refundOrigins.help: Tied to a recorded installment payment. The policy check runs against that payment and is frozen onto the request.

refundOrigins.label: Raised by hand
refundOrigins.help: No ledger row to reverse — a duplicate transfer someone sent us, an overpayment, an order taken off-platform. It names its own payee and carries no policy check, because an empty check would read as a passed one.

refundGrounds.label: Duplicate charge
refundGrounds.help: The same amount taken twice for the same thing. The clearest ground there is.

refundGrounds.label: Cancelled before activation
refundGrounds.help: Paid, then cancelled before the membership was switched on. Nothing was consumed.

refundGrounds.label: Overpayment
refundGrounds.help: More money arrived than was ever owed. Common on manual transfers.

refundGrounds.label: Service failure
refundGrounds.help: We did not deliver. Needs the detail, because the approver is being asked to accept a fault.

refundGrounds.label: Other / goodwill
refundGrounds.help: Not a permitted ground. The request is still accepted and still reaches the approver — it is framed as an exception, not blocked.

refundPolicy.$comment: Full refunds only, for the same reason payments are full: a partial refund implies a partly-paid installment, which the 1:1 rule says cannot exist. The check FRAMES the approval, it does not block it — hard-blocking every out-of-window refund means a genuine duplicate cannot be processed at all.

$comment_refundStates: APPROVAL MOVES NO MONEY. It authorises a transfer a human makes in the bank; the refund is only `paid` when somebody records that transfer with its reference. The gap between `approved` and `paid` is real money owed and not yet sent, and the Overview counts it.

metricDefinitions.label: Collected
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ installment payments in the period − Σ reversals − Σ refunds paid
metricDefinitions.caution: Money that arrived. Installments that are due, and invoices nobody has paid, are not in this figure — the first has not happened and the second is a demand.

metricDefinitions.label: Salary cost
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ net paid on runs whose month falls in the period
metricDefinitions.caution: Net paid to people, not cost to company. Employer PF and gratuity are not in this seed, so this is what left the bank, not what the team costs.

metricDefinitions.label: Other spend
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ recorded transactions with direction out and a tag whose kind is not excluded
metricDefinitions.caution: Excluded tags — taxes and statutory — are real money leaving that is deliberately not in the operating picture. They are counted in cash out, never here.

metricDefinitions.label: Other income
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ recorded transactions with direction in
metricDefinitions.caution: Never revenue. All three permitted credits are flagged non-revenue, so this figure can never be mistaken for a sale.

metricDefinitions.label: Refunds paid
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ refunds whose state is paid, by settlement date
metricDefinitions.caution: Approved and not yet transferred is NOT in this figure. That gap is shown separately, because it is money owed and still sitting in the account.

metricDefinitions.label: Approved, not sent
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ refunds in state approved with no settlement
metricDefinitions.caution: Money the company has agreed to return and has not returned. It is still in the bank balance and it is not the company's.

metricDefinitions.label: Net
metricDefinitions.caution: Say net, never profit. Full cost allocation does not exist here — no depreciation, no employer contributions, no accruals.

metricDefinitions.label: Due next 30 days
metricDefinitions.formula: Σ the next payable installment of each active subscription, due within 30 days of asOf
metricDefinitions.caution: Expected, not earned, and only what is genuinely in front of each customer: one installment per subscription, never the rows behind it, and nothing at all from a subscription that is already defaulting — the last attempt at that money did not clear.

metricDefinitions.label: Fail to pay
metricDefinitions.caution: Money that was owed and did not arrive, with the reason recorded on each one. It is not written off — it is uncollected.

metricDefinitions.label: Matched to bank
metricDefinitions.formula: rows carrying a bankLineId ÷ rows in an imported statement window
metricDefinitions.caution: Completeness, not correctness. A high figure says the ledger and the bank agree on what exists, and says nothing about whether a row was tagged right.

kpiDefinitions.label: MRR
kpiDefinitions.formula: Σ (subscription total ÷ cycle months) over active subscriptions
kpiDefinitions.caution: A level, read at a moment, never a rate summed over a period. Defaulting subscriptions are excluded the moment an installment fails — counting them is how MRR quietly becomes fiction.

kpiDefinitions.label: ARPU
kpiDefinitions.caution: Null, not zero, when there are no active subscriptions. A denominator of nothing has no average.

kpiDefinitions.label: Collection rate
kpiDefinitions.formula: installments paid ÷ (installments paid + fail to pay), by due date in the period
kpiDefinitions.caution: Installments still `due` are excluded — they are not late yet, and including them would make every current month look like a failure.

kpiDefinitions.label: Fail to pay rate
kpiDefinitions.formula: installments fail_to_pay ÷ installments due or past due in the period
kpiDefinitions.caution: The single number that says whether the installment model is working. A gateway decline and a passed due date are counted the same here; the record screen separates them.

kpiDefinitions.label: Salary to collected
kpiDefinitions.formula: salary cost ÷ collected, over the same period
kpiDefinitions.caution: Above 100% means the team cost more than the month collected. Meaningful only over a closed month — a part-month salary run against a part-month of collection compares nothing.

kpiDefinitions.label: Cost per head
kpiDefinitions.caution: Net paid per person, not CTC per person. A month with a loss-of-pay adjustment will read low for a reason that has nothing to do with pay scales.

kpiDefinitions.label: Monthly burn
kpiDefinitions.formula: salary cost + other spend + refunds paid, over the period
kpiDefinitions.caution: Cash leaving, excluding tagged-excluded statutory payments. It is not the same as expenses: an expense recognised is not money gone.

kpiDefinitions.label: Net margin
kpiDefinitions.caution: Not profit margin. The word profit needs full cost allocation, which this module does not have.

kpiDefinitions.label: Refund rate
kpiDefinitions.formula: refunds paid ÷ collected, over the period
kpiDefinitions.caution: A refund is dated when the transfer was made, not when the original payment was. A refund of a July payment lands in the month it was actually sent.

kpiDefinitions.label: Runway
kpiDefinitions.caution: Needs a reconciled cash balance and several closed months of burn. Neither exists in this seed, so it returns null — a placeholder here is a decision made on a wrong number.

kpiDefinitions.label: New customers
kpiDefinitions.formula: distinct customers whose first installment payment falls in the period
kpiDefinitions.caution: First payment, not first subscription and not signup. A renewal by an existing customer is not a new customer.

kpiDefinitions.label: CAC
kpiDefinitions.caution: Null, never zero, in a period with no new customer — dividing by nothing is not free acquisition. Only reinvestment-tagged spend is in the numerator, which is why the tag has to be right.

kpiDefinitions.label: Website share
kpiDefinitions.formula: collected from website-sourced subscriptions ÷ total collected
kpiDefinitions.caution: Channel mix by money, not by count. One large sales-closed deal will move this more than ten small self-serve ones.

roles.finance: Record a subscription and its installments · record an installment payment · open a salary run and issue slips · record a company expense or income · create a tag · request a refund · record a refund transfer · close a period
roles.superAdmin: Reverse a payment or a transaction · mark a salary run paid · approve or decline a refund · deactivate a tag

openDecisions.title: Recorded is what happened
openDecisions.position: Every row in this module exists because something occurred. There is no verification step and no state meaning "recorded but not yet believed". Fail to pay is not an exception: it records a decline or a passed due date, and stores the evidence.

openDecisions.title: Posted is immutable
openDecisions.position: Nothing is edited or deleted. A correction is a counter-entry referencing the original, with an actor and a reason.

openDecisions.title: One installment, one payment
openDecisions.position: The installment is the unit that gets paid, in full. There is no part-payment field because there is no part-paid installment to record it against.

openDecisions.title: Customer money has one door
openDecisions.position: Revenue enters only as a subscription installment. The three hand-keyable credits are all flagged non-revenue.

openDecisions.title: Tags are custom, kinds are not
openDecisions.position: Anyone with edit rights creates a tag. The kind is chosen at creation and decides where the money lands. A tag is deactivated, never deleted.

openDecisions.title: Cash view, not accrual
openDecisions.position: Everything here is cash in and cash out on the value date. There is no accrual P&L, no deferred revenue and no revenue recognition schedule — a twelve-month subscription paid up front reads as collected in the month it was paid.

openDecisions.title: Bank matching is simulated
openDecisions.position: A statement import exists and can be run once against a seeded file. There is no live bank feed, so "matched to bank" is a demonstration of the mechanism, not a live figure.

openDecisions.title: Who approves what
openDecisions.position: Super Admin approves refunds and marks a salary run paid. A bill is required above ₹25,000 before a period closes.

openDecisions.title: Salary scope
openDecisions.position: Salaries A/C records accounts, monthly runs and slips. It does NOT do statutory filing, PF challans, gratuity, leave balances or reimbursements, and it does not compute TDS — the figure is entered, not derived.

openDecisions.title: Employer cost is not in salary cost
openDecisions.position: Salary cost is net paid to people. Employer PF, gratuity accrual and insurance are not modelled, so cost per head understates true cost to company.

openDecisions.title: Runway is not shown
openDecisions.position: It needs a reconciled cash balance and several closed months of burn, neither of which this seed carries. It returns null with the reason on screen rather than a number nobody should act on.

openDecisions.title: Tax is a summary, not a return
openDecisions.position: GST is shown as a summary of what was invoiced. It is not a return, it does not net input credit, and it is not a filing.

openDecisions.title: Net, never profit
openDecisions.position: Screens say contribution and net. Profit needs full cost allocation, which does not exist here.

openDecisions.title: One supply, several invoices
openDecisions.position: The sales chain raises one tax invoice per installment, so one subscription appears as several invoices. The tax summary shows it plainly and it awaits CA sign-off.

openDecisions.title: Failed installments are not chased from here
openDecisions.position: Fail to pay is recorded and surfaced. Retrying a charge, sending a dunning email and suspending the membership all belong to other modules; Finance shows the fact and links out.

openDecisions.title: Deductions are flat, and statutory PF is not
openDecisions.position: Loss of pay pro-rates earnings and leaves every deduction alone, because deductions are typed on the account and this module does not decide which of them are proportional. In law employee PF is 12% of basic and falls with a pro-rated basic, so a loss-of-pay slip overstates PF and understates net. Fixing it means marking a component proportional or flat when it is typed, which is a schema decision and a payroll-policy one, not a rendering fix.

$comment_payrollDefinitions: THE PAYROLL FACE HAS ITS OWN METRIC LIST, deliberately not folded into metricDefinitions above: the KPI tab renders EVERY entry in kpiDefinitions grouped by its `group`, so a payroll figure added there would appear, unasked, on a page about subscriptions and refunds. A second list — payrollKpiDefinitions, six decision metrics with year-on-year arrows — was here and is DELETED with the block it annotated: the Salaries A/C analytics tab was cut back to four totals and three charts because the metrics, and the two wide tables under them, were the half of the page that made it confusing rather than the half that made it useful. Every figure that survived still prints its formula and its caution behind an i, which is the only defence against one number meaning two things six months apart.

payrollMetricDefinitions.label: Payroll, the year
payrollMetricDefinitions.formula: Σ (earnings + incentives) over every slip issued in the financial year
payrollMetricDefinitions.caution: COST, not cash: it is what the payroll came to before deductions, so it does not match what left the bank. Deductions are money withheld and owed onward, not money saved — the figure a bank statement matches is Paid out, beside this one. THE YEAR IS JANUARY TO DECEMBER, the calendar year and NOT the April-to-March one that the books, TDS and PF all close on, so this total will not match a filed return. The two spans are close enough to be mistaken for each other and far enough apart to matter.

payrollMetricDefinitions.label: Paid out
payrollMetricDefinitions.formula: Σ net on slips stamped paid, over the financial year
payrollMetricDefinitions.caution: What actually left the accounts. A slip issued and not yet paid is not in it, which is why this and Payroll, the year differ for any month still open.

payrollMetricDefinitions.label: Still owed
payrollMetricDefinitions.formula: Σ net on unpaid slips + Σ net on held slips, over the financial year
payrollMetricDefinitions.caution: Held and unpaid are added here because both are money not yet gone, but they are NOT the same thing and the chart separates them: unpaid is a payment that has not happened, held is one somebody stopped for a stated reason. A total that hides the difference reports a dispute as arrears.

payrollMetricDefinitions.label: Incentives
payrollMetricDefinitions.formula: Σ incentive lines over every slip issued in the financial year
payrollMetricDefinitions.caution: Variable pay only — money earned for something achieved, never pro-rated by loss of pay. A fixed monthly allowance called Performance allowance is NOT in this figure: it is committed pay under a hopeful name, and it sits in the fixed half where it belongs.

payrollMetricDefinitions.label: On the payroll
payrollMetricDefinitions.formula: count of salary accounts that are open, as at now
payrollMetricDefinitions.caution: THE ONLY FIGURE HERE COUNTED FROM ACCOUNTS RATHER THAN SLIPS, and the only one that moves the moment a salary account is opened. Every other figure on this page is derived from slips, so a new account changes none of them until a run is opened and paid — correct for money, and no feedback at all for somebody who has just added a person. The monthly figure beside it is what a run opened today would cost before deductions: a COMMITMENT, not a cost, and it is not part of any total on this page.
